The model skeleton provides an auditor with insights into the specific model class used, the architecture, and the interactions between different components of the AI system, including expected inputs and outputs. It allows the auditor to understand the structure and relationships within the AI system, offering a more interpretable view of how the system operates.

In contrast, the training procedure includes details about the model class, objective function, hyperparameter tuning, and quality checks, serving as a roadmap for the development of the AI system. While access to the training procedure can help auditors perform sanity checks and understand the design choices made during development, it does not guarantee that the resulting models will behave similarly, as the ultimate behavior of the model depends on various factors beyond the training procedure.

Thus, while the model skeleton focuses on the architecture and operational aspects of the AI system, the training procedure emphasizes the development process and decisions made, which may not directly translate to the model's behavior.
